leaders.notes: CityU's president(s) during this ~1996-2006 window could not be identified from publicly available sources; the university's online historical archives do not document leadership prior to Lee Gorsuch's 2006 appointment. Left as a placeholder rather than fabricating a name.

Served as UAA chancellor 1994-2004 before joining CityU in 2006 (a short gap between the two roles was not clarified in sources found). Announced retirement in June 2012, effective June 30, 2013; recognized for advancing academic rigor and global partnerships.

leaders.priorTitle: VP Business Operations & Regional VP, Business & Operations
leaders.notes: Appointed effective July 1, 2013; announced retirement effective June 30, 2016 after only three years. During his tenure CityU grew enrollment and gained doctoral-level accreditation. Next role after CityU not found.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor of Business and Administration
leaders.nextRole: New role within National University System
leaders.notes: Appointed effective October 1, 2016. Led a financial turnaround (raised Dept. of Education composite score, restored positive cashflow) and oversaw CityU's 50th anniversary (2023). Took a leave in 2022 during which COO Christopher Bryan served as interim president, then resumed; departed the presidency for good in 2024, at which point Bryan again became interim president.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Operating Officer & Chief Financial Officer
leaders.nextRole: Chief Operating Officer & Chief Financial Officer
leaders.notes: Named interim president effective September 2, 2024, continuing his COO/CFO duties; he had also briefly served as interim president once before, in 2022. Served as bridge leader until Suzanne Walsh's arrival in July 2025.

Named CityU's 5th president, effective July 1, 2025; the first woman and first person of color to lead the university in its 50-plus-year history. Previously led Bennett College and held roles at the Gates Foundation, Lumina Foundation, and Heinz Endowments.

Long-serving 14th president of Clarke College (a Sisters of Charity of the Blessed Virgin Mary institution); named to the role January 27, 1984, and retired June 30, 2006. Term start pre-dates this index's 1996 research window but is included since she was serving through the window's opening.
Began her term July 1, 2006; oversaw the 2010 transition from Clarke College to Clarke University. Succeeded by Thom Chesney in 2019.

Clarke's 16th president; led the university through the COVID-19 pandemic before resigning (reported at the time as taking a personal sabbatical). Later became president of Southwestern College in New Mexico.

Clarke's 17th president; joined as interim president in January 2023 and was named permanent president in July 2024. Resigned in late October 2025, about 16 months after being made permanent, with Vice President for Academic Affairs Yvonne Zimmerman named interim successor. A short leadership gap between Chesney's 2022 departure and Lamkin's January 2023 start was not clearly documented in sources found.

Named interim president in late October 2025 following Fletcher Lamkin's resignation, while the Board of Trustees searches for a permanent replacement. Joined Clarke in 2023 as Dean of Academic Affairs and became VP for Academic Affairs in 2024; previously spent 15 years at Methodist Theological School in Ohio.

Colorado Technical University is a for-profit institution (owned by Career Education Corporation, later renamed Perdoceo Education Corporation, since 2003) whose campus-level president succession is not well documented in public news archives, press releases, or Wikipedia for this period. Founder Robert (Bob) Turkisher was first president from the school's 1965 founding; CTU gained university status in 1995. No reliable named successor could be identified until Andrew Hurst by 2014. Left as a placeholder rather than fabricating a name.

Served as President of Colorado Technical University under parent Career Education Corporation starting around April 2014. End date is approximate (inferred from a February 2021 leadership announcement referencing his tenure); his next role was not confirmed in sources found.

Appointed University President of Colorado Technical University in January 2022, after 3 years as COO and over 12 years total at CTU. Also serves as Senior Vice President at parent Perdoceo Education. Exact leadership status between Hurst's ~2021 departure and Baskel's January 2022 appointment (interim gap) was not confirmed.

Second president of the institution (then Christ College Irvine, renamed Concordia University Irvine in 1993), succeeding founding president Charles Manske (who stepped down to a faculty role in 1979). Term start pre-dates this index's 1996 window but is included since he was serving through the window's opening; end year of 1998 is inferred from successor J.A.O. Preus III's start date.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Faculty / Professor of Systematic Theology
leaders.nextRole: Executive Vice President of Mission Advancement
leaders.notes: Third president of Concordia University Irvine, 1998-2009. Resigned September 23, 2009. Later served as North American Liaison for Fundacion Educacional Concordia after leaving Bethesda in 2014. Died in 2022.

leaders.notes: Fourth president of Concordia University Irvine, appointed 2010. Announced his retirement; exact retirement date not confirmed in sources found (site access blocked), but inferred as 2019 based on successor Michael Thomas's January 2020 start.
